notes: Specified the logjam-pressure mechanism for the fleet keeper, superseding the D022 item-3 logjam ESCAPE (dispatch-a-conflicting-task-anyway) that the operator rejected on 2026-08-20 01:07 as a one-writer violation. Deliverable docs/infra/fleet-keeper-design.md is the keeper's authoritative algorithm: NORMAL (cap C = FLEET_CAP, default 5) vs PRESSURED (a conflict-blocked 'next' mutation task anchors; effective cap C_eff = max(1, C - drops) where drops increments by one per task leaving in_progress while the same anchor stays blocked; floor 1, proved both necessary and automatic). The keeper never dispatches a task whose holds intersect any running task's holds (the one-writer invariant) NOR the anchor's holds under pressure; only holds-free/conflict-free work refills freed slots while pressured. Priority is the bundle-header priority=N (0-99, default 50, tie-break added) plus a waiting=1 bump that makes a task 'next' regardless of priority (the operator's bump use case). Impatience model recommended completion-driven only (clock-free dispatch arithmetic; the lone clock is telemetry waiting_since). Long-holder logjam escape recommended as option (c) holder-timeout flag (FLEET_LOGJAM_FLAG, default 60 min) writing untracked/fleet-keeper.logjam.flag + log line, human acts via option (b) manual managent verbs, option (a) documented as the unbounded worst-case baseline; no silent preemption. Model cooldown (FLEET_MODEL_ALLOW/DENY) binds the pressure path because the gate lives inside eligibility. Eight control arms specified (a-h: drop-then-solo, conflict-free-still-runs, conflict-never-dispatches, no-blocked-next, holds-free-immediate, model-cooldown-binds, logjam-flag, bump) on scratch store+repo (MANAGENT_STORE + FLEET_ROOT + --test-root, T427/T476), red-first, to be wired into zig build test by the implementing worker. No register change (claims: []). Inbox loop (T352): polled bin/managent inbox T500 --ack at task open and before done; empty throughout, no D0NN directives read.
